name: LeverUp USD
oneLiner: lvUSD is LeverUp's liquidity-layer stablecoin on Monad, minted against USDC and MON inside the perpetuals trading engine rather than a standard reserve.
collateral: USDC and MON collateral supporting LeverUp's liquidity-layer stablecoin for perpetuals and margin trading
pegMechanism: Synthetic stablecoin used inside LeverUp's Monad liquidity layer, with mint, burn, and redemption mechanics tied to the protocol's collateral and trading engine

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: lvUSD is tied to a managed perpetuals liquidity layer on a new chain; available sources do not prove a direct blacklist function, but admin and protocol-control risk remain unresolved.

notices.title: Perpetuals liquidity-layer stablecoin
notices.message: lvUSD is included through CoinGecko price and market-cap coverage, but its collateral and redemption model are tied to LeverUp's trading system rather than a conventional issuer reserve.

mintAuthority.summary: lvUSD is minted inside LeverUp's Virtual Market Making Vault (VMMV) trading engine on Monad when traders open positions against USDC/MON collateral; minting is controlled by the protocol's trading-engine contracts under a project multisig rather than a permissionless or renounced system.

controls.label: LeverUp VMMV trading-engine (minter)
controls.capDescription: lvUSD is auto-minted by the LeverUp trading engine when a trader opens a position using USDC/MON collateral (one independent pool per collateral); all positions are denominated and settled in lvUSD inside the VMMV, so supply is tied to open collateralized positions.
controls.evidence: LeverUp docs state the system automatically mints lvUSD when a trader opens a position with USDC (or MON) collateral, with each token managed in its own trading pool under the VMMV design.

controls.label: LeverUp protocol admin multisig
controls.capDescription: A LeverUp project multisig administers the managed liquidity layer and trading engine on a new chain; specific signer set, threshold, and pause/upgrade powers are unresolved.
controls.evidence: lvUSD metadata flags governance as a multisig over a managed perpetuals liquidity layer on Monad; the docs do not prove a renounced or permissionless minter, leaving admin control unresolved.

review.evidence: LeverUp documentation describes lvUSD as an engine-minted liquidity-layer stablecoin auto-issued against USDC/MON collateral inside the VMMV; the project is managed by a multisig on Monad and does not document a renounced or permissionless mint authority.
review.sourceFreeRationale: Engine-mint mechanism confirmed from LeverUp docs; the controlling multisig's signer set, threshold, and upgrade/pause powers were not independently resolved on-chain.
unresolvedQuestions: Resolve the LeverUp admin multisig (signers, threshold) and the trading-engine/token upgrade and pause authority before raising confidence.
